title: Move version_info to libui and remove epan dependency

notes.body:
Before:

```
$ build/run/editcap --version | egrep -i zlib
with zlib 1.2.11.
GLib 2.58.3, with zlib 1.2.11, with locale C, binary plugins supported (0
$ 
```

After:
```
$ build/run/editcap --version | egrep -i zlib
$ 
```

This needs to be fixed (preferably without giving that information twice), as editcap *does* use zlib - as does every other program that uses libwiretap, as libwiretap uses zlib to read compressed files.

Right, thanks for pointing that out. That's the main reason VERSION_INFO_LIBS was created, I remember now, vaguely.

I don't immediately see a sane alternative to having a VERSION_INFO_LIBS if we insist on showing the dependency versions for every utility (instead of only programs using epan) so I will probably give up on removing that.

@guyharris I reverted the change that removed the Zlib version. Can you review this again?

Does it still make sense to move version_info to ui? The VERSION_INFO_LIBS construct irks me.

> I reverted the change that removed the Zlib version. Can you review this again?

It works.

> Does it still make sense to move version_info to ui? The VERSION_INFO_LIBS construct irks me.

The "cleanest" solution, for some value of "clean", might be to have common version-string code that includes "add this string to the compiled-with version set" and "add this string to the running-with version set", where "set" means "no duplicates", with each library, and the main program, calling those APIs; the version-string code would make sure that, for example, separate Zlib strings from libwireshark and libwiretap would only be stored once in the set if they're identical (which they should be).  Other APIs would generate the final compiled-with string and the final running-with strings once the sets are complete.

(I put "cleanest" in scare quotes because a duplicate-string-elimination mechanism seems like a bit much for generating version strings, but so it goes.)

That should either end up in libui or libwsutil; for now, putting version_info.[ch] in libui sounds reasonable as showing the version information is a UI operation.
Thanks. I agree with your points. "Cleanest" but a bit over-kill.

commits_data.title: Move version_info.[ch] to ui/
commits_data.message:
Move version_info.[ch] to ui/

Version info is an aspect of UI implementation so move it to
a more appropriate place, such as ui/. This also helps declutter
the top-level.

A static library is appropriate to encapsulate the dependencies
as private and it is better supported by CMake than object libraries.

Also version_info.h should not be installed as a public header.

commits_data.title: epan: Remove dependency on version_info object library
commits_data.message:
epan: Remove dependency on version_info object library

Dependending on version_info is unnecessary and forces an epan
rebuild every time the git commit id changes, which can be slow,
especially with LTO enabled, and again is unnecessary.

Printing the VCS version to the TLS debug log is a minor convenience
that doesn't justify the cost to relink epan with every commit.
